meta.description: Synthetic binary A-B convex hull: why Matbench Discovery scores crystal stability as a decision (F1, DAF) rather than as energy regression (MAE).
meta.units: eV/atom throughout unless a key says meV
meta.hull_algorithm: Andrew monotone chain, lower chain only; cross-checked against scipy.spatial.ConvexHull
meta.threshold_note: Matbench Discovery's headline threshold is E_hull <= 0; it also reports a sweep over the threshold, mirrored in threshold_sweep.
meta.protocol: primary = hull rebuilt from predicted energies (competing phases move too); secondary = predicted energy against the fixed true hull, closer to the benchmark's use of the Materials Project hull

exp3_mae_f1_inversion.predictor_P: truth + N(0, 25 meV/atom), same error everywhere
exp3_mae_f1_inversion.predictor_Q: truth + N(0, 2 meV/atom + 0.35 * E_hull_true), accurate near the hull, sloppy far above it

exp4_error_cost.note: A false positive spends one DFT relaxation or one synthesis attempt: bounded, observed, recoverable. A false negative silently deletes a real material from the campaign: unbounded and invisible, because nothing downstream ever reports it.

findings.f1_not_superlinear_in_sigma: FALSIFIED EXPECTATION: the peak noise-resolved elasticity is |dlogF1/dlogsigma| = 0.815 +/- 0.038 (2-sigma upper bound 0.890), below MAE's constant slope of 1, so F1 does not decay faster than linearly in sigma. Single-interval estimates scatter up to 0.921, which is consistent with the smoothed value given Monte-Carlo error and is not evidence of a super-linear region.
findings.f1_not_a_power_law: F1's local elasticity ranges 0.064 to 0.815 while MAE's is pinned at 1.000; F1 falls from 0.9 to 0.3 across only 33.2 meV/atom of MAE.
findings.predicted_hull_shrinks: Self-consistent protocol: predicted stable count falls 10.6 -> 5.2 as sigma grows, opposite to the naive expectation that noise manufactures spurious stable phases.
findings.protocol_matters: At sigma = 200 meV/atom the fixed-hull protocol predicts 63.6 stable structures against 5.2 for the self-consistent one: same energies, opposite failure mode.
findings.mae_f1_inversion: Predictor P beats Q on MAE (20.0 vs 48.5 meV/atom) and loses on F1 (0.454 vs 0.824) in 96.5% of trials.
